chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
I wrote to him asking him about a question, so he wrote back to me:
Verily Allah says: 'Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but it is He who causes them to be deceived,' up to His saying: '[a] way.'
They are not from the progeny of the Messenger of Allah, and they are not from the faithful believers, and they are not from the Muslims.
They manifest belief outwardly but hide disbelief and rejection [of faith] in their hearts.

key_terms.الْمُنَافِقُونَ: Hypocrites, those who feign faith while concealing disbelief
key_terms.عِتْرَةُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The progeny/family of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida define the characteristics of hypocrites in relation to the Prophet's progeny and true believers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the ontological distinction of the hypocrites (al-munafiqun) by citing Surah An-Nisa, asserting they are separate from the Ahl al-Bayt and true believers. He characterizes them as those who outwardly display faith while concealing disbelief, a condition that warrants the divine curse mentioned in the verse. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the purity of the Prophet's progeny as distinct from the class of hypocrites who feign piety.
